# Destination Local Contract — v1

Inspect [the plan](../plan.md) and [the spec](../spec.md) for behavior and ownership. This artifact defines local Rust/Tauri DTO boundaries, not HTTP endpoints.

| Boundary | Input | Output / invariant |
|---|---|---|
| destination snapshot | active session ID | session ID, cancel generation, version, phase, capability, selection, badge metadata; no text |
| destination menu | current session/version | opaque entry tokens, foreground-first non-Handy entry, deduplicated windowed apps, FrontmostAtEnd; no window titles |
| choose destination | session ID, expected version, opaque token or FrontmostAtEnd | updated snapshot/version before Inserting; stale/closed/frozen request refuses unchanged |
| activation | frozen application identity, cancel generation, monotonic deadline | app_closed, activation_failed or dispatch permission; never launch/retry/fallback |
| pre-dispatch guard | frozen resolved identity and generation | check immediately after configured delay, before first key/text/script; fail means zero new dispatch |
| settings get | output key return_to_dictation_app | same 008 success envelope/revision, value and capability availability/reason |
| settings set | bool, expected revision when supplied | 008 shared commit; unsupported→unavailable/5, invalid→validation_failed/2, stale→revision_conflict/3 |
| recovery access | outcome/session opaque transcript_ref | retained final text for trusted native consumer while current; expired reference explicitly unavailable |

`InsertionOutcome` fields: session_id, cancel_generation, outcome_id (dedup key), target optional stable identity, destination_source, status, reason optional, history_status, history_entry_id optional, transcript_ref optional, completed_at. Status: insertion_attempted/failed/skipped/cancelled. Reason: app_closed/activation_failed/insertion_failed. History: saved/not_saved/failed from actual WAV/save result. No verified field flag and no public plaintext event.

Producer: terminal destination orchestration in actions.rs; consumers: 007 clipboard recovery, 009 Enter policy, 010 reason/recovery bubble. Registration is optional; missing feature never prevents terminal outcome. Native registry stores transcript separately from UI event DTO. Session/version/cancel generation reject late/duplicate delivery. Reason presenter capability and acknowledgement transfer display ownership to 010; preserve minimum ≥4 s visibility and visible-overlay fallback if no ack. Style-none before 010 has no bubble; no certified reason presentation claimed then.

Configuration envelope is exactly `{ok:true,revision:N,data:{...}}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}`, newline once on stdout under --json, diagnostics on stderr. Existing 008 exit mapping remains 0 success, 1 persistence/internal, 2 usage/validation/conflict/limit, 3 revision conflict, 4 not found, 5 unavailable. No alternative lock, writer or transport. Pure reads/no-op preserve revision; failed validation/capability/CAS leaves disk unchanged.

# Implementation Plan: Destination Application

## Summary

Capture one application identity per dictation in a Rust destination manager, allow explicit session changes through a nonactivating badge/menu, then asynchronously activate and verify the application before delegating to the existing insertion method; publish truthful outcomes and preserve conditional history/recovery evidence.

Inspect [the functional source](spec.md) for FR-001–FR-006, AC-001–AC-008 and SC-001–SC-003. Scope **L**: six FR, native macOS/Windows activation, shared insertion lifecycle and 007/009/010 consumers. Deliver after 008 and before 007/009/010. This document is a plan; no application code, native compatibility or visual certification has been produced.

## Technical Context

| Aspect | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Native | Existing Rust 2021, Tauri 2.11.5, Tokio | Keep platform and manager boundaries from manifests |
| Frontend | React 18, TypeScript, Zustand, i18next, existing Tailwind/CSS | Retain overlay and output settings components |
| macOS workspace | Existing objc2-app-kit 0.3, NSWorkspace/NSRunningApplication | Native identity/activation; no shell/AppleScript process |
| Windows workspace | Existing windows 0.61.3 Win32 bindings | Foreground HWND→PID→AUMID or executable path; native activation |
| Storage | 008 settings service for one boolean; existing history SQLite path | No new database table, separate volatile dictation state |
| Concurrency | Session manager + async activation worker + brief main-thread native calls | No sleep, polling loop or blocking worker join on native UI thread |
| Test levels | Cargo unit/integration; Bun adapter; Playwright components; real native harness | Browser mocks cannot prove OS focus/activation |
| Infrastructure | Local OS APIs only | No cloud provisioning or secret required |

Inspect [start/paste lifecycle](../../../src-tauri/src/actions.rs), [coordinator](../../../src-tauri/src/transcription_coordinator.rs), [insertion methods](../../../src-tauri/src/clipboard.rs), [reliable paste](../../../src-tauri/src/paste_tx/mod.rs), [native overlay](../../../src-tauri/src/overlay.rs), [frontend overlay](../../../src/overlay/RecordingOverlay.tsx) and [settings](../../../src-tauri/src/settings.rs) before implementing. At planning time actions.rs saves history only under `wav_saved` and queues `utils::paste` on `run_on_main_thread`; clipboard.rs sleeps before/after a paste and owns current auto-submit and clipboard policy. These are integration constraints, not proofs of insertion.

Inspect [008's approved plan](../008-settings-cli/plan.md) as the framework reference; do not revise it. Reuse its exact `SettingDescriptor`, `SettingsMutation`, `SettingsSnapshot`, `Revision`, `PublicSettings`, `OperationRequest`, `SettingsError`, `StoreLocator`, `SettingsRepository`, `LiveSettingsEffects`, `read_snapshot` and `commit_mutation` names and `settings_service/{descriptor.rs,validation.rs,protocol.rs,errors.rs,store.rs,transaction.rs,live.rs,domains/mod.rs,domains/output.rs}` layout. No independent settings writer, lock, revision counter, transport or renderer is introduced by 006.

## Constitution Check

| Principle | Explicit check |
|---|---|
| Existing native/frontend boundaries | PASS: Rust owns destination/lifecycle; frontend renders typed snapshots and requests choices |
| Manifest-derived stack and managers | PASS: use existing objc2/windows/Tauri; review needed feature flags, no new inference/cloud dependency |
| Tool availability distinct from runtime | PASS: commands below are resolved only; native and UI evidence remains required later |
| Changed behavior specified first | PASS: six FR and eight AC mapped; spec semantics untouched by planning |
| Meaningful tests and source verification | PASS: real session logic, fake OS ports, real file/CLI/native boundary tests, no mocked manager under test |
| Naming and project tooling | PASS: keep existing Rust module conventions and TS filenames; new UI/artifact names kebab-case; retain ESLint/Prettier/Bun rather than changing toolchain |
| i18n and data boundaries | PASS: all badge, toggle, accessibility and reason text through translation keys; no transcript/window-title broadcast or logs above debug |

## Architecture Decisions

### Session and application identity

`DestinationManager` owns `DestinationSession {session_id, cancel_generation, version, phase, return_enabled, support, selection, captured_at}`. `selection` is `FrontmostAtEnd` or `Application {identity, display_name, icon_ref, captured_pid, source}`; `source` is captured or badge (009 will add its own PIN policy). Destination is an application, never a saved field/window. Keep last-active-window semantics to the OS, no AX classification in 006.

Capture when a recording actually starts, including a queued coordinator press when it drains, not when a key press was remembered while busy. Snapshot support and setting, read frontmost before showing any Handy surface, and create/commit the session only on successful recording start. Discard tentative state on mic/model/start failure. Capture work is bounded <50 ms, including the native main-thread hop; delay/capture failure is a capability failure with the old insertion path and explicit unavailable reason, not a fabricated destination. Do not enumerate all windows or load icons synchronously on this path. Cache small icon assets by app identity and finish badge rendering asynchronously; snapshot its icon reference/availability rather than holding UI/native objects across threads. Native spike must prove this tuple and latency.

macOS identity is bundle identifier; PID and process start identity defend against PID reuse. Windows prefers AUMID, otherwise canonical executable path; keep HWND only as an activation hint, not field-level authority. Revalidate HWND→PID→identity at activation. Exclude Handy and its panels/helpers by own process identity. Same app clicked is a no-op. Restart: if original PID is gone, resolve a running instance with the same stable identity; prefer a still-valid captured instance, otherwise one unambiguous matching instance. Multiple ambiguous matches fail closed as activation_failed; do not select an unrelated process by display name. Closed identity is app_closed, never auto-launch. Icons/names have native fallback handling without inventing a target.

Freeze `return_enabled` and capability for each accepted dictation so CLI/UI changes affect the next dictation, as Story 5 specifies. Capture and selection stay unchanged through recording, processing and AI except explicit badge choices. A mutation requires exact session_id/version and phase before Inserting; insertion entry atomically freezes selection, closes any menu and rejects late choices. Cancellation invalidates the session/generation; late native replies and stale UI events cannot activate or insert into the next session.

### Platform support and menu enumeration

`WorkspacePort` exposes `capability`, `frontmost`, `running_windowed_apps`, `resolve_identity`, `activate_once`, `observe_frontmost`. Native calls return typed snapshots, not framework objects. macOS uses NSWorkspace frontmost/running apps and NSRunningApplication; Windows uses GetForegroundWindow/GetWindowThreadProcessId, AUMID/path lookup, EnumWindows and SetForegroundWindow. Inspect [Apple frontmostApplication](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsworkspace/frontmostapplication) and [NSRunningApplication](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsrunningapplication) as informative API context. Inspect [Microsoft SetForegroundWindow restrictions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setforegroundwindow) as informative context: an activation request is not proof of foreground success.

Linux is explicitly unsupported; macOS/Windows become unsupported when frontmost cannot be read. Distinguish a readable Handy foreground (supported, no destination) from no readable foreground. On supported systems the default boolean is true. Unsupported state is `{available:false, reason}` with old insertion behavior, hidden badge and disabled toggle with localized explanation; no persisted forced false and no silent write. Setting attempts on unsupported systems return 008 `unavailable`/exit 5, including both true and false; type-invalid inputs return validation_failed/2 first. Reads are nonmutating and report value plus support. A failure after a valid destination was captured is activation_failed/app_closed, never a switch to the legacy frontmost path.

At menu-open read frontmost before touching surface focus, list that non-Handy app first, then deduplicated other running applications with user windows, and finally Frontmost app at the end. Exclude daemon/helper/windowless entries from the remaining list; do not expose window titles. Current chosen destination is marked. Entries use opaque manager tokens; stale/closed choice is rejected without changing session, refresh list, and localized feedback; never accept caller PID/name alone. Clicking outside dismisses unchanged. Badge/menu is pointer-operated per approved spec, while settings toggle supports Tab/Space and a spoken label.

### Activation and insertion threading

The orchestrator performs: check cancellation → freeze chosen destination → retain final text/history status → skip activation if paste_method=none → resolve target → request activation once → await foreground condition bounded by monotonic 1 s → schedule existing method → recheck cancellation and target immediately before actual first dispatch. The 1 s deadline bounds activation request scheduling and foreground observation only. A late activation callback cannot authorize insertion. Successful foreground observation within the deadline creates a session/generation-bound activation authorization; configured insertion delays occur afterwards and are not charged to the activation deadline. At actual dispatch after such a delay, require a fresh foreground and cancellation check; never reuse a stale foreground observation or reactivate on failure. OS notifications may wake observation, with bounded async sampling as fallback. Brief AppKit/native requests run on main thread via returned channels; all deadline waiting happens on worker/Tokio. Never join a worker, sleep, enumerate all apps or poll for 1 s inside run_on_main_thread.

A single activation call, no retry on failed final recheck. Already-frontmost still rechecked. Deadline 999/1000/1001 ms boundaries tested with injected Clock; timeout/cancellation invalidates activation callbacks. Test observation at 100 ms with paste_delay_ms=1500: valid foreground/cancellation checks after the preserved delay permit dispatch; focus loss during that delay prevents it without reactivation. Off/unsupported/no destination/FrontmostAtEnd retains current insertion policy and does not activate a captured app. PasteMethod::None can retain existing clipboard output policy, but has `skipped` outcome, never `insertion_attempted` and never activates. Empty final text/cancel produces no activation/input.

Retain all configured method behaviors (direct, ctrl_v, shift_insert, ctrl_shift_v, external_script, reliable-paste), delays, trailing-space, existing clipboard handling and auto-submit semantics. Introduce a thin `InsertionPort` adapter around clipboard.rs, adding an optional pre-dispatch guard, not a replacement method algorithm. Its guard runs **after paste_delay_ms**, immediately before first emitted key/text or external-script launch, with no clipboard-policy side effects for an unavailable destination. When feasible check at subsequent direct-typing chunk boundaries to abort on lost focus; the final unavoidable OS race remains documented. Do not advertise atomic focus+injection or verified field text.

Separate timing from UI ownership: async orchestration schedules existing bounded native method calls where required; configured activation wait adds no main-thread freeze. Existing long direct-typing/external-script/delay paths are already a responsiveness risk; Step 1 measures them and Step 4 extracts waits and process waiting to workers while keeping thread-bound key/clipboard calls brief, preserving output bytes, method choice and delays. Such scheduling changes are technical integration, not a new insertion method. If the selected existing adapter cannot preserve these boundaries, block its implementation proof rather than claim responsive UI.

006 does not add Enter: current legacy auto-submit remains inside existing adapter until 009 takes ownership. Provide 009 with the frozen target identity and attempted outcome; its later change must route both legacy and reliable-paste auto-submit through its own policy to prevent duplicate or wrong-target Enter. 007 alone owns restoration/recovery-window policy; destination never restores or changes clipboard settings. A method's success can be asynchronous enqueue success (reliable paste), not a field verification. Method errors after partial delivery cannot undo characters; no fallback to another application or retry is performed.

### Outcome, conservation and staged recovery

Native `InsertionOutcome` v1: `{session_id, cancel_generation, outcome_id, target: Option<ApplicationIdentity>, destination_source, status, reason, history_status, history_entry_id, transcript_ref, completed_at}`. Status is `insertion_attempted | failed | skipped | cancelled`; failure reason is `app_closed | activation_failed | insertion_failed`. `history_status` is saved/not_saved/failed, assigned only from actual WAV/save_entry result. `transcript_ref` is an opaque native reference, never plaintext in an event. No `verified` success flag. UI receives metadata only through typed `destination-changed` and `insertion-outcome`; trusted native consumers access retained text by current session reference. Event/consumer dedup uses outcome_id, no text-based deduplication.

Producer is destination orchestration at the former paste completion in actions.rs, exactly once per terminal session. 007 consumes outcomes to manage its clipboard recovery window (its future internal cancel-without-restore API is left to 007, used by 010 Copy); 009 consumes target and attempted status for Enter; 010 consumes failed/uncertain outcomes and the reference for its bubble and field classification. Hand off to registered consumers, not a dependency on an absent feature. Consumer registry declares its reason-presentation capability. Avoid broadcasting transcript via app-wide events/logs. Contract tests verify optional/missing consumers, duplicate and stale events.

History guarantee is explicitly conditional as AC-005/SC-002 require: keep existing WAV-gated save, never claim history when WAV or save_entry fails. Story 4's history assertion is exercised with successful saving as its precondition; spec is not silently rewritten. Preserve the final text in the native recovery slot on destination failure even when history fails; keep latest unresolved outcome until superseded by a later final result, explicit consumer release or process exit. This bounded volatile slot is technical handoff storage, not durable history or a new recovery feature; old references fail explicitly. No restart/crash survival is claimed without a successful history save. A later successful dictation can supersede it; log/notice history failure separately without transcript. This limitation must be stated truthfully in native proof.

While 010 is absent, visible-overlay failures use a dedicated reason state in the indicator for **at least 4 s measured from visible presentation**; do not run the unconditional hide-after-paste path first. Existing generation guard extends to reason timers so a previous failure cannot hide a new recording. If another recording starts during these 4 s, keep reason in the dedicated nonactivating surface until its minimum display duration instead of overwriting/hiding it. App closed, activation failed and insertion failed have distinct localized text; text preservation description reflects actual history status. Tray returns idle independently of reason lifetime.

**006→010 ownership:** once 010 advertises reason presentation, delegate the failure reason/transcript reference to its bubble for all styles, including overlay none, and suppress the duplicate indicator reason. 010 inherits the ≥4 s minimum reason visibility obligation from 006; its AC-001 replaces the surface, not conservation or truthful status. Require a 010 consumer acknowledgement before suppressing 006's visible fallback. No handler/acknowledgement → fallback ≥4 s when an overlay is enabled. With style none before 010 ships, emit typed outcome plus existing paste-error feedback to the settings listener and retain text/history; there is no visible recovery bubble yet. Document that staged limitation; do not enable an overlay against the user's none setting or invent a certification of the absent bubble. 007/010 recovery behavior is tested when each consumer arrives.

### Settings and local contracts

Add `return_to_dictation_app: bool` descriptor to 008's existing output domain and PublicSettings projection, rather than registering a second output domain. Commands: `handy settings output get return_to_dictation_app --json`, `handy settings output set return_to_dictation_app true|false --json`, also generic get/set via that descriptor. UI command uses the same SettingsMutation and pure validation/capability guard; read_snapshot/commit_mutation use 008's same latest-state validation, expected revision, lock, durable persist and LiveSettingsEffects. Do not persist session destination, icon, PID or selection in AppSettings. No-op does not increment; success increments once; stale CAS/error leaves store unchanged. Domain output help extends additively and keeps method/clipboard keys separate.

Return exactly 008 envelopes `{ok:true,revision:N,data:{...}}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` and existing exit mapping 0/1/2/3/4/5. Unsupported set: `unavailable`, reason/platform in details, exit 5, no revision change. Invalid bool: validation_failed/2; stale CAS: revision_conflict/3 with current_revision. Success is configuration only, never insertion evidence. Startup missing-key default/migration runs only through 008 service; pure reads do not write. UI receives settings-changed revision/key names and discards older refreshes. Live availability may change independently of boolean; a private capability update refreshes disabled state without a settings revision write.

New local contract artifact is [destination contract](contracts/destination-contract.md): typed session commands, outcomes, availability and settings command matrix. No new network endpoint and no openapi.yaml.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Prove native feasibility before feature wiring

**Prerequisite:** 008 implemented with its service and current spec/plan gates READY; program UI contract design gate completed before UI code.
**Required inputs:** Current overlay/clipboard/action source, target OS versions, test applications, approved one-pass geometry, native workspace APIs.
**Action:** New `scripts/destination-native-proof.ts` orchestrates real app runs and evidence collection; new `src-tauri/tests/destination_platform.rs` exercises injectable native boundary adapters. Spike macOS NSPanel badge resizing and a separate nonactivating `destination_menu` webview panel (can_become_key_window=false); Windows no-activate HWND/WebView2 surface using WS_EX_NOACTIVATE and WM_MOUSEACTIVATE handling. Prove pointer open/select/dismiss preserves keyboard focus, last-active-window/Space activation, capture tuple <50 ms, ≤1 s activation, delay-time final recheck and UI heartbeat. Include existing slow direct/external-script/clipboard delays before selecting safe worker scheduling. No normal NSMenu tracking loop which captures keyboard. ## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** When a dictation starts and the frontmost application is not Handy, Handy records its identity (bundle identifier on macOS; application user model ID on Windows when available, otherwise executable path), display name, icon and process id. Application switches during the recording, processing and AI step do not change it. When Handy is frontmost, no destination is recorded.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** With "Return to the dictation's application" on (default on where supported), before insertion Handy activates the destination and waits until it is frontmost, for at most 1 second and without freezing Handy's interface, re-checks that it is still frontmost immediately before inserting (a failed re-check counts as an activation failure, without retry), then runs the configured insertion method unchanged. With the paste method "none" no application is activated. With the setting off, or without a destination, insertion targets the frontmost application as today.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 5

## Architecture Decisions

### Entry point and Windows console

Use `CliArgs::try_parse_from` before any Tauri builder, specta export, model/audio manager, portable mutating initialization or single-instance callback. `settings` runs and exits here; all old invocations retain their existing run branch. Accept both JSON placements and deduplicate them. Mixed settings with recording, startup, transcription/model/device/list/repeat flags is usage_error (2); `--debug` and `--json` remain compatible. Parser failures with JSON requested use the same envelope renderer without echoing raw values. JSON help is `{ok:true,revision:N,data:{help:...}}`, human help remains readable; obtain revision using the same non-mutating read path.

Windows decision: retain one `handy.exe`, use the **console PE subsystem** so cmd/PowerShell wait and capture exits, preserve inherited redirected handles, and attach to the parent console only if no valid console/pipe handles exist. For GUI launch, detach before Tauri and hide only a newly allocated console owned solely by this process, never the parent's console. Embed detached consoleAllocationPolicy on Windows 11 24H2+; on earlier supported Windows use early native hide/FreeConsole and a regression gate for launch flash, autostart, old flags and installer behavior. AttachConsole alone in a GUI-subsystem binary cannot establish synchronous shell execution. Inspect [Microsoft console allocation policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/console-allocation-policy) and [AttachConsole](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/attachconsole) as external technical context. Step 1 must prove this choice on the oldest supported Windows and 24H2 before final wiring; a persistent console, disrupted redirected output or incorrect exit is a release blocker. No console shim is silently introduced; failure requires a separately approved alternative, not a claim of platform support.

### Paths, storage and revision

Extract side-effect-free StoreLocator from portable initialization. Read the portable marker without upgrading it or creating Data; resolve installed user app-data using the configured identifier com.pais.handy and OS APIs, not guessed HOME strings. For nonexistent paths, canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor, append validated components and reject symlink/reparse aliases that cross user boundaries. Lock identity survives atomic store replacement: lock the stable sibling lock file, never the replaced JSON inode.

SettingsRepository reads fresh disk bytes under settings.lock; missing store gives defaults/revision 0. Read only salvage/migrate/merge defaults in memory, never save, create settings_store.json, upgrade portable marker or increment revision. Startup takes the same lock and explicitly commits any initialization/migration change once. Older stores with no revision start at 0; first changed commit is 1. Preserve a valid top-level revision through payload salvage; malformed existing revision or unrecoverable revision continuity refuses writes with persistence_failed rather than reset-and-CAS. Entire unreadable JSON reports defaults with warning for read recovery, but cannot be overwritten automatically; explicit supported recovery is outside this feature. Semantic no-op after normalization does not write or increment; migrations persisted by startup are real writes. Reject revision overflow before native effects. Never silently reset the counter.

Commit a typed mutation/patch against the newly loaded settings, not the caller's stale AppSettings snapshot. Validate the whole candidate and dependencies, compare normalized persisted values (including secret changes, excluding runtime overrides), increment once, serialize the entire preserved store object to a private same-directory temporary file, flush/sync, atomically replace and sync the parent directory on Unix (Windows replacement APIs and durable flush). Crash injection must observe old or new complete generation, never partial JSON. Disable plugin-store ownership/autosave/exit-save for this particular settings file; a reload alone cannot prevent a delayed old cache write. Other plugin stores remain unchanged. A compatibility AppHandle adapter reads the service snapshot; it cannot write the settings file independently.

### All surfaces and live effects

Migrate every writer before CLI set becomes reachable, including get_settings migration/default stores, shortcut fallback/reset commands, UI setters, audio/model selection repairs, model switches and history retention. The inventory is the actual call-site scan, not a hand-selected subset. Replace write_settings(AppSettings) with `commit_mutation` closures/typed patches and propagate Result. Preexisting runtime-only flags and forced-disable-updater remain overrides, never persisted writes.

Inject LiveSettingsEffects for native validation/preparation, shortcut registration, audio/model reconfiguration, autostart, theme/log settings and settings-changed. Worker transaction serializes prepare/validate → durable persist → publish snapshot → apply live effects → notify. Prepare any fallible reversible native change before commit; compensate it on persistence failure. For effects that can fail after durable commit, do not falsely return validation_failed: return internal_error with details `{outcome:"committed", current_revision:N, field:...}`, keep committed data authoritative and reconcile live state before accepting another affected mutation. Timeout still reports outcome unknown to the caller. P0 tests require invalid/refused values and failed preparation leave both disk and revision unchanged, and injected effect failure never yields a success with stale shortcuts. UI native command adapters become async workers where needed; never wait for a worker holding the transaction lock from the main thread. Event contains revision and changed key names only, no secret values; the existing listener refreshes and discards older refresh responses by revision.

### Routing, startup fence and legacy compatibility

New app acquires a per-user/store instance lease before loading settings, under the settings lock, publishes its private endpoint before releasing startup ownership, and keeps the lease until shutdown. A headless writer acquires settings.lock, then checks lease/endpoint/legacy state again; GUI startup and headless mutation cannot pass each other unnoticed. The lease is separate from the transaction lock; a busy or starting owner never means offline permission. A stale PID/endpoint is reclaimable only after OS liveness/ownership proof and protected endpoint removal; ambiguous access errors return unavailable with no write.

| OS | Private request channel / peer verification | Older instance detection and headless-start exclusion |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | Short AF_UNIX path in owner-only runtime directory (0700), socket 0600; verify peer effective UID with getpeereid | Inspect legacy `/tmp/com_pais_handy_si.sock` owner and process/socket liveness without invoking its callback. Offline mutation reserves legacy address under lock; fail closed on any ambiguous existing socket. A compatibility guard captures startup probes for deferred handoff without executing UI callbacks while reservation is held |
| Linux | AF_UNIX under validated XDG_RUNTIME_DIR user directory or short private fallback; SO_PEERCRED UID | Query session DBus `com.pais.handy.SingleInstance` via NameHasOwner/GetNameOwner, not ExecuteCallback. Offline guard temporarily owns that name, disallowing replacement, to exclude old startup |
| Windows | Named pipe keyed by SID+store hash, protected DACL for current logon SID, reject remote clients and verify client token; no Everyone ACL | Open/query legacy `com.pais.handy-sim` mutex and `com.pais.handy-sic`/`com.pais.handy-siw` target without sending WM_COPYDATA. Offline guard reserves legacy mutex plus hidden nonactivating top-level compatibility target with the exact legacy class/title, because FindWindowW cannot locate a message-only target and mutex-only does not stop this plugin's startup branch; no displayed window or Tauri initialization |

Inspect the locked [macOS plugin source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/macos.rs), [Windows source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/windows.rs) and [Linux source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/linux.rs). Cargo.lock currently resolves 2.4.0, not the manifest minimum 2.3.2. Names/protocol must be recalculated if that dependency changes. For legacy identities which do not expose store identity, conservative refusal is preferable to a write; process token/UID and path evidence must identify user scope. Never connect/send an empty command to an old singleton: macOS empty streams still invoke the show-window callback. No assumed socket absence authorizes a write.

Legacy reservations are held by a private **offline guard worker of the same executable**, never by an inert sink. The CLI starts that worker only for offline mutations through an internal authenticated inherited-handle entry point (not a public CLI flag). The worker acquires the transaction lock, rechecks instance/legacy ownership, installs the exact legacy protocol adapters, performs the typed mutation through the same service and returns its envelope to the parent CLI. It owns all reservation handles for their entire lifetime; there is no cross-process lock-handle migration. Old singleton startup messages use the legacy protocol and become queued **activation/control intents**, not settings requests. The protocol does not carry trustworthy original sender PID/executable identity on Windows (SendMessageW uses wParam=0 and the sender ignores its return). Do not claim authentication of that legacy sender or require an impossible rejection acknowledgement. The guard derives replay target exclusively from its own trusted current Handy executable path, exactly as existing singleton forwarding targets the current owner rather than selecting argv[0]. It parses only the existing control/startup flags and cwd needed to preserve behavior; it never launches an executable named by incoming argv[0], executes a script payload, applies settings mutations, returns settings data or accepts secret-bearing input through this compatibility path. The settings channel itself remains exclusively the authenticated UID/SID socket/pipe described above. Any legacy compatibility security restrictions must preserve existing official requests; the native security review separately evaluates this inherited activation/control surface, including another user's desktop/session.

Windows receives WM_COPYDATA on a hidden top-level native message loop, Linux temporarily serves the existing ExecuteCallback interface, and macOS reads the NUL-framed stream to EOF. Persist each validated official invocation into a private ordered handoff spool before acknowledging where the legacy protocol permits acknowledgement; retain messages during filesystem backpressure instead of an inert success/no-op. The macOS sender waits for no acknowledgement, so receipt means stream acceptance, not sender-visible delivery; retain a complete frame durably before closing the accepted stream. No queue-full/drop rule is introduced for valid official invocations: use private spool files and bounded per-frame memory with backpressure. Failure to prepare the spool or guard before commit returns persistence_failed/unavailable to the settings CLI without changing settings; never enable the offline writer while the capture surface is unusable.

Once the CLI has flushed its single result and exited, the worker observes parent exit via an OS process handle/liveness port, drains accepted legacy frames, removes its legacy identities under the transaction lock, and replays queued invocations in arrival order into the trusted current Handy executable with validated argv/cwd. First queued startup uses its original startup flags; later invocations use normal singleton forwarding. The real app thus loads the fully committed store, and existing toggle/post-process/cancel precedence remains unchanged. The worker never initializes Tauri, displays UI or loads a model; replay is the separately initiated legacy invocation after settings has exited. Keep a consumed-ID/spawn receipt per queue entry; distinct invocations are never deduplicated by identical text. A process crash around spawn cannot guarantee exactly-once replay: mark that entry's outcome unknown and require explicit recovery, never blind relaunch. Durable pending frames survive worker crash; replay recovery must be explicit and cannot silently execute stale recording commands on a later unrelated CLI invocation. A handoff failure reports the pending/unknown entry and committed settings revision in private diagnostics, not successful legacy delivery. Step 1 must prove normal non-lossy handoff and separate every fault/unknown path, with no success claimed for unobserved legacy delivery. This worker/spool is a technical necessity for safe legacy exclusion, not a new user-facing daemon or second CLI executable.


Offline legacy reservation is a critical spike: native adapters must prove old-start exclusion, normal non-lossy queued handoff and truthful fault outcomes, cleanup, same-user scoping and no visible UI effects. If any OS cannot provide this, disable offline mutations there and report a release blocker against AC-005; do not certify complete delivery. Requests to a running new app carry protocol version, user/store identity, opaque request ID, typed operation, expected revision and dry_run. Bound UTF-8 frame size to 1 MiB, reject malformed/oversized input without raw dumps. Domain imports have the same bounded technical limit until a future owner explicitly defines another. Requests contain no raw argv. Use a monotonic 5 s end-to-end response deadline; transport/persistence/lock wait counts toward it. Successful M1 reads must finish ≤2 s; timeout failures are recorded separately, never counted as successful reads. No fallback write or blind automatic retry after submission/timeout; reread revision and value first. Late replies cannot resurrect an expired request.

### Descriptors, output domain and contract rendering

Descriptor inventory covers every AppSettings field, with wire type, enum/range, mutable/read-only, secret/presence projection, owning domain, runtime effect and validator. Build a reviewed manifest plus an independent test inventory from serialized default settings and all UI adapters; a descriptor omission fails, not silently hides a setting. Existing scalar settings are generic-settable except internal fields (schema, revision, onboarding/migration markers, manager-only model state) and provider configuration, which remain read-only from CLI. API-key fields are secret and never generic-settable. Lists/maps return validation_failed naming their owning domain command, plus `not available in this build` when unregistered; include owning command even when unavailable to satisfy AC-002. Optional values have descriptor-defined null handling; non-null boolean accepts exactly true/false, numeric parses without overflow, enums use existing serde values, strings preserve bytes without trimming meaningful content.

Redact via explicit public projection, never AppSettings Serialize or Debug. `post_process_api_keys` becomes per-provider `{present:boolean}` only; nested/future secrets inherit the rule. All stdout, stderr, parse errors, IPC diagnostics and logs sanitize raw candidate values. Public errors use stable English text and object details, with field/issues where applicable; no OS trace, raw document or credential in details. Reject `paste_method=invalid_method` identically via UI and CLI rather than existing default-to-ctrl_v behavior. UI maps code+field to i18n keys, falling back to a translated generic error, not free-text parsing.

`output get [KEY]` and `output set KEY VALUE` delegate to the same descriptors for existing paste_method, clipboard_handling, auto_submit, auto_submit_key, paste_delay_ms, paste_delay_after_ms, reliable_paste, typing_tool, external_script_path and append_trailing_space. Existing enum values remain unchanged: ctrl_v/direct/none/shift_insert/ctrl_shift_v/external_script; dont_modify/copy_to_clipboard; enter/ctrl_enter/cmd_enter. This is configuration, not insertion execution. Do not mix destination 006/009, method and clipboard recovery 007. A request's committed output settings do not prove text insertion.

Domain trait registers command schema/help, file/`-` input, pure parsing/validation, preview, typed patch and export formatter. Valid dry-run loads latest revision, validates fully, emits preview/revision with exit 0, and does not persist or call effects. Invalid dry-run returns validation_failed/2 with issues, no success preview. `-` explicitly requests stdin, never prompts; non-UTF-8 text returns byte offset in details. Export `-` human mode is raw exchange content only; JSON is data.content. Fixture domain proves bulk merge/replace/atomic all-or-nothing and live-only unavailable behavior; it never appears in production help.

| Result | Exit |
|---|---|
| success | 0 |
| persistence_failed, internal_error | 1 |
| usage_error, validation_failed, shortcut_conflict, limit_exceeded | 2 |
| revision_conflict (`details.current_revision`) | 3 |
| not_found | 4 |
| unavailable (timeout: `details.outcome=unknown`) | 5 |

The enum+single renderer owns this mapping. Every JSON operation emits exactly one `{ok:true,revision:N,data:...}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` followed by newline; diagnostics go to stderr. No newly introduced HTTP endpoints: OpenAPI would misrepresent local IPC. Contract is the typed DTO/JSON-schema and command matrix in Step 2; no openapi.yaml generated.

```gherkin

Deadline 999/1000/1001 ms boundaries tested with injected Clock; timeout/cancellation invalidates activation callbacks. New app acquires a per-user/store instance lease before loading settings, under the settings lock, publishes its private endpoint before releasing startup ownership, and keeps the lease until shutdown. A headless writer acquires settings.lock, then checks lease/endpoint/legacy state again; GUI startup and headless mutation cannot pass each other unnoticed. | macOS | Short AF_UNIX path in owner-only runtime directory (0700), socket 0600; verify peer effective UID with getpeereid | Inspect legacy `/tmp/com_pais_handy_si.sock` owner and process/socket liveness without invoking its callback. The CLI starts that worker only for offline mutations through an internal authenticated inherited-handle entry point (not a public CLI flag). The worker acquires the transaction lock, rechecks instance/legacy ownership, installs the exact legacy protocol adapters, performs the typed mutation through the same service and returns its envelope to the parent CLI. It owns all reservation handles for their entire lifetime; there is no cross-process lock-handle migration. The protocol does not carry trustworthy original sender PID/executable identity on Windows (SendMessageW uses wParam=0 and the sender ignores its return). The settings channel itself remains exclusively the authenticated UID/SID socket/pipe described above. Windows receives WM_COPYDATA on a hidden top-level native message loop, Linux temporarily serves the existing ExecuteCallback interface, and macOS reads the NUL-framed stream to EOF. The macOS sender waits for no acknowledgement, so receipt means stream acceptance, not sender-visible delivery; retain a complete frame durably before closing the accepted stream.
